facts.text: Bath was named after Bath, England, reflecting settlers' aspirations for prosperity and refinement.
Founded in 1818, Bath evolved from a pioneer settlement into a desirable place to live, balancing historic preservation and modern convenience.
Hale Farm and Village, a living history museum, showcases 19th‑century life through restored homes, working farms, and interactive demonstrations.
Bath’s oldest park, Bath Community Park, opened in 1968 and spans 41 acres of wooded trails, tennis and basketball courts, and picnic shelters.
The township’s first regular fire station organized in 1922 replaced bucket brigades, marking a shift to organized emergency services.
Bath’s cemeteries, including several historic ones, offer insight into early settlers’ lives and serve as quiet reminders of the area’s deep roots.
